theory.intro: Our number system is decimal, based on tens, but time is **sexagesimal**, based on sixties. A time in hours, minutes and seconds must therefore be rewritten before it is used as a decimal number of hours.
facts: To go **to** decimal hours: divide the minutes by $60$, divide the seconds by $3600$, then add these to the whole hours.
To go **from** decimal hours: multiply the decimal part by $60$ for minutes, then multiply any leftover decimal by $60$ again for seconds.
Useful values: $0.25$ h $=15$ min, $0.5$ h $=30$ min, $0.75$ h $=45$ min.
$2$ h $37$ min is **not** $2.37$ h — it is $2.61\dot{6}$ h, because $37\div60=0.61\dot{6}$.
A calculator's sexagesimal (DMS) controls can convert between the two forms. Enter hours, minutes and seconds in the correct form before converting.
steps: Convert the remaining part: divide minutes by $60$ for a decimal, or multiply a decimal by $60$ for minutes.
If seconds are involved, divide by $3600$ or multiply the leftover by $60$ once more.

workedExamples.question_text:
Write these times as decimal hours.
(a) $5$ h $24$ min
(b) $47$ min
workedExamples.solution_text:
Divide minutes by $60$ and add any whole hours.
(a) $5+\frac{24}{60}=5.4$ h.
(b) $\frac{47}{60}=0.78\dot3$ h. The $3$ repeats; keep this exact recurring decimal.

workedExamples.question_text: Convert $3$ h $12$ min $45$ s to decimal hours.

Write these times in hours and minutes.
(a) $6.35$ h
(b) $0.65$ h
workedExamples.solution_text:
Keep any whole hours; multiply the decimal part by $60$.
(a) $0.35\times60=21$ min, so $6.35$ h $=6$ h $21$ min.
(b) $0.65\times60=39$ min, so $0.65$ h $=39$ min.

workedExamples.question_text: Convert $4.2375$ h to hours, minutes and seconds.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Keep $4$ whole hours.
$0.2375\times60=14.25$ min.
Keep $14$ whole minutes, then convert the remaining fraction:
$0.25\times60=15$ s.
The time is $4$ h $14$ min $15$ s.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Convert $2.\dot6$ h to hours and minutes.
(b) Convert $7$ min $30$ s to decimal hours.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $0.\dot6=\frac23$.
$\frac23\times60=40$ min, so $2.\dot6$ h $=2$ h $40$ min.
Keep the exact repeating value instead of rounding it first.
(b) $\frac7{60}+\frac{30}{3600}=\frac18=0.125$ h.

development.question_text: Convert $245$ minutes to hours in decimal form.
Convert $128$ minutes to hours in decimal form.
Convert $1$ hour $33$ minutes $27$ seconds to hours in decimal form.
Convert $13$ minutes $25$ seconds to hours in decimal form.
Convert $1.875$ hours to hours, minutes and seconds.
development.solution_text:
$1.875\text{ h}$
$=1\text{ h}+0.875\times60\text{ min}$
$=1\text{ h}+52.5\text{ min}$
$=1\text{ h }52\text{ min}+0.5\times60\text{ s}$
$=1\text{ h }52\text{ min }30\text{ s}$

development.question_text: Convert $8.125$ hours to hours, minutes and seconds.
development.solution_text:
$8.125\text{ h}$
$=8\text{ h}+0.125\times60\text{ min}$
$=8\text{ h}+7.5\text{ min}$
$=8\text{ h }7\text{ min}+0.5\times60\text{ s}$
$=8\text{ h }7\text{ min }30\text{ s}$

development.question_text: Convert $0.281$ hours to minutes and seconds.
development.solution_text:
$0.281\text{ h}$
$=0.281\times60\text{ min}$
$=16.86\text{ min}$
$=16\text{ min}+0.86\times60\text{ s}$
$=16\text{ min }51.6\text{ s}$
